just-in-time.title: Just in Time
just-in-time.researchTrigger: BRO-4989 checker #3: model 233% vs reported recoupment May 2026
just-in-time.notes: Review request about data already in commercial.json. Do not apply; verify, edit commercial.json by hand, then delete this row. Stored $600K/week is a Reddit estimate (u/Boring_Waltz_9545, 2026-05-19). No trade report of the running cost was found. Derived, not reported: with the $12.5M capitalization (Playbill/Variety) and the weekly grosses on file, the model recoups in mid-March to late March 2026 at $790K-$840K/week and has not recouped by now at $850K+. Playbill reported recoupment on 2026-05-18, which brackets the cost at about $800K-$850K/week (+33% to +42% over $600K). At $600K the model says 233% returned today; at $800K-$850K it says about 92-120% (credit counted) or 72-100% (credit not counted). Context: Broadway Journal (Philip Boroff, 2025-06-05) said a company chart showed recoupment of $9.4M production costs soon after Labor Day 2025 at a $1.2M weekly gross, including up to $3M state tax credit. Actual recoupment came about 8 months later, on a $12.5M figure, which also points to higher costs than $600K. Wanted: a cited weekly running cost or break-even (trade press, producer statement, or SEC/offering filing).

book-of-mormon-2011.title: The Book of Mormon
book-of-mormon-2011.capitalizationSource: NYT ArtsBeat blog, producers confirmed ~$11.4 million capitalization upon recoupment announcement
book-of-mormon-2011.recoupedSource: NYT ArtsBeat (archive.nytimes.com) reported November 29, 2011 that the show recouped after nine months; Hollywood Reporter also reported recoupment after eight months
book-of-mormon-2011.notes: The Book of Mormon opened March 24, 2011 and recouped its ~$11.4 million capitalization within approximately 8–9 months. It has run continuously since 2011, making it a decade-defining long-running mega-hit with extraordinary investor returns. Crain's New York Business reported it outperformed Amazon, Google, Netflix, and the Dow Jones for investors. Clearly qualifies as a Miracle by longevity and profit multiple criteria.

wicked-2003.title: Wicked
wicked-2003.capitalizationSource: Playbill article dated 2004-12-21 states 'whopping $14 million capitalization'; corroborated by Broadway Journal
wicked-2003.recoupedSource: Playbill article dated 2004-12-21 headlined 'Wicked Within Days of Recouping Investment', stating it would recoup by end of year; Broadway Journal corroborates 'announced recouping in December 2004'
wicked-2003.notes: Wicked opened October 30, 2003 at the Gershwin Theatre with a $14 million capitalization. It recouped its entire investment in approximately 14 months, by December 2004. The show has run for over 20 years on Broadway and is widely regarded as one of Broadway's all-time mega-hits, qualifying it clearly as a Miracle. Weekly running costs are noted to be 'well over $1 million' but no precise figure is explicitly stated.

the-lion-king-1997.title: The Lion King
the-lion-king-1997.notes: The Lion King opened November 13, 1997 at the Minskoff Theatre and remains one of the longest-running and highest-grossing productions in Broadway history, widely documented as having surpassed $9 billion in global gross across productions. It clearly qualifies as a Miracle by any reasonable standard — decades-long run, extraordinary profit multiples, a defining phenomenon of Broadway's modern era. However, none of the evidence gathered contains explicit figures for Broadway capitalization, weekly running costs, or a confirmed recoupment date.
